title: Electronics Predictive Maintenance
thesis: Snowflake turns sensor readings from a synthetic Vietnamese SMT fleet into uptime KPIs, 7-day failure-risk scores, vibration anomalies and grounded AI answers, all on curated dynamic tables.

talking_points: Uptime, unplanned stops, MTBF and spare coverage for 20 SMT machines across 5 locations.
Every KPI is a numerator over a denominator in a curated dynamic table, so it can be traced back to machine-day rows.
The downtime chart shows which root causes cost the most hours.
tabs.call_out: One governed set of maintenance KPIs, traceable to source rows

transition.line: Which machines are likely to fail next?

talking_points: Snowflake ML classification scores each machine's probability of failure in the next 7 days.
The holdout line shows precision and recall on the most recent days, against the base rate.
Anomaly detection flags vibration outliers per machine, and the forecast projects fleet downtime for 14 days.
tabs.call_out: Honest, evaluated ML inside the data platform

talking_points: Parts on order and spare coverage frame the response capacity.
PM compliance against yield by machine shows where discipline and output move together; it is an association, not proof of cause.
The action memo drafts three prioritised actions from the KPI, downtime and risk tables only.
tabs.call_out: Grounded draft actions, with a human in the loop

transition.line: What happens when a machine alarms right now?

talking_points: Live readings land in RAW.LIVE_TELEMETRY, from the simulator or from AWS IoT Core through Snowpipe.
The Snowflake alert logs ALARM readings with an SOP hint and the machine's current risk band, then emails the engineer.
tabs.call_out: From alarm to action in one platform

talking_points: The Cortex Agent uses Cortex Analyst over the semantic view for metrics, and Cortex Search over 14 synthetic SOPs.
Each answer shows the generated SQL and the SOPs it cited.

transition.line: Here is how it is built.

talking_points: Two builds share one core: Snowflake only, or AWS + Snowflake (IoT Core, Bedrock, QuickSight and Amazon Q).
Everything shown is synthetic demo data, rebuilt reproducibly from the repo.
tabs.call_out: One governed core, with an optional AWS edge
